schema_note: schema 2 adds the cells: the column vocabulary, the per-column check against the printed totals, and per record `cells` (committed) beside `cells_first_pass` (read, unreconciled). Schema 1 records carry names only.
division: S. W. Sherman (as written into the printed heading)
read_pass: names and cells (T-0527, piece 5 of 7 of T-0495)
line_count_note: 31 ruled lines, all 31 carrying a name. THE COVERAGE INVENTORY SAID 33 `to the nearest line` AND THE SHEET CARRIES 31, counted twice and then measured. The body is ruled vertically only; its two horizontal rules stand at y=577 (below the printed column heads) and y=2911 (the closing rule, which slants down to the right). 2911-577 = 2334 px divided by 31 lines is 75.3 px per line. Independently, a two-parameter grid was fitted by least squares to the y of 108 measured ink blobs in the cell columns -- the enumerator's tally marks, which are isolated and unambiguous, as against the name ink, whose ascenders and descenders bias a centroid -- and answers pitch 75.20 with line 1 at y=670, within a tenth of a pixel per line of the figure the rules give. An earlier fit made to the NAME ink alone answered 76.0 and put a thirty-first line at y=2962, below the closing rule; it is superseded, and the disagreement is recorded rather than hidden. The last two lines are crowded: line 30's marks stand at y~2828 and line 31's at y~2884, about 45 px above the uniform grid, which is what a last entry squeezed in above the closing rule looks like.

margin_annotation.position: written vertically up the LEFT margin of the leaf, outside the NAMES column, at x~170-260, spanning y~1450-2130 -- beside body lines about 11 to 20. Read by rotating the crop 90 degrees.
margin_annotation.why_it_matters: this is the only thing anywhere on the exposure that names the place. The printed heading names the enumerator's division and the state blank is filled `Illinois`; neither says Chicago. T-0527 asked for the annotation to be recorded as a finding in its own right, and it reads `Chicago Precinct` -- the civil division, not the bare town name.

header_note: the printed heading reads `(No. 4.) SCHEDULE of the whole number of persons within the division allotted to ____` with `S. W. Sherman` written into the blank, and the printed page number `239` at the top right.
form_note: The left (names) sheet of the 1840 population schedule. Columns as printed, left to right: NAMES OF HEADS OF FAMILIES; thirteen FREE WHITE PERSONS - MALES age bands; thirteen FREE WHITE PERSONS - FEMALES age bands; six FREE COLORED PERSONS - MALES bands; six FREE COLORED PERSONS - FEMALES bands.
grid_note: HOW THE CELLS WERE LOCATED. The vertical rules on this exposure are far fainter than on 33SQ-GYYJ-6V and a single high-passed darkness profile returns them mixed with paper streaking. Twenty-five rules that stand clear were assigned their column index and fitted by least squares, answering x = 690.9 + 80.81 n with rms 3.29 px and a largest residual of 7.2 px; the same pitch carries on through the FREE COLORED block to the leaf's right edge, which the detected rules there confirm. Boundaries are therefore taken as x = 691 + 80.81 n for n = 0..38: the NAMES column closes at 691, the thirteen male bands run to 1741, the thirteen female bands to 2792, and the twelve coloured bands to 3762. Every reading was made on a grid overlay drawn at those boundaries and at the fitted line centres.
cells_note: Seventeen columns carry a footed figure and ALL SEVENTEEN CLOSE EXACTLY: males 13, 11, 4, 34, 10, 5, 1, 1, 1 and females 6, 7, 8, 9, 21, 2, 5, 1, 1. Two columns cannot be closed and are recorded as such rather than counted as closures. THE FOURTH MALE BAND (15 under 20) has a footing glyph so faded that at 8x it will not resolve between 4, 6 and 7; the line-by-line read is 6 and is committed unchecked. THE FIFTH FEMALE BAND (30 under 40) carries TWO figures: `26` on the footing line and `21` written immediately below it in the same ink. Read column-alone at 2x against the line grid the column carries 21 -- a 2 on line 1, seventeen single strokes, and a 2 on line 31 -- so `21` is the enumerator's own correction of `26`, and the reading reproduces the corrected figure independently. 147 persons on 31 lines.
free_colored_note: The FREE COLORED block is blank on all 31 lines except ONE mark, on line 15, and its footing row is blank from column 27 to column 38 -- so the block carries no printed check at all. The mark itself is written hard against the printed rule at x=3358, which is the boundary between column 33 (free colored males, 24 under 36) and column 34 (free colored females, 10 under 24); its body lies to the RIGHT of the rule and it is committed to column 34, with column 33 recorded here as a live alternative that the sheet gives no way to settle. Everything else in the block is swept and empty, and that zero is committed as evidence rather than left absent.
name_note: This sheet's ink is thinner and more faded than 33SQ-GYYJ-6V's, and the lower third (lines 22 to 27) is the faintest stretch of it. Where more than one surname fits, every candidate is named in the record's own note; `as_read` carries `[?]` at a letter POSITION that cannot be resolved (T-0397). Superscript abbreviations are transcribed as written (`Geo`, `Saml`) and expanded only in `normalized`. Lines 3 and 4 carry the same surname on consecutive lines, which is a neighbour relation in enumeration order and is NOT recorded as a household or family link.
ipums_note: No IPUMS serial is attached on this sheet; T-0504 does that across all three groups by the age-band fingerprint.
